prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates a near foreground—the camera wearer’s arms/body and the counter or papers, generally within about 0.2–0.8 m—from people and fixtures farther ahead, roughly 1–3 m away. Across the five frames, the nearest bright regions shift from the left and lower foreground toward the centre and then the right/lower foreground as the wearer turns or moves along the counter; the person ahead remains farther away and moves from near centre to the right side of view. It clarifies overlapping depth layers that are ambiguous in RGB, including that the counter is in front of the standing person and that dark background gaps lie behind nearby people and objects. Exact metric distances are not encoded, and several depth boundaries around arms, reflective screens, papers, and frame edges look smoothed or inconsistent, so the metre estimates and fine occlusions are unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies partial people in frames 2–3 and 5, a TV/display in frame 4, and laptops plus a bottle and small counter objects in frame 5; these are mainly in front of the wearer, with the people about 1–2.5 m away and the counter objects roughly 0.5–1.2 m away. The person masks move from the left side in frame 2 to a large central foreground occlusion in frame 3, then appear toward the right in frame 5, while the display occupies the upper-left/central area in frame 4. It makes object identity and overlap clearer than RGB—for example, laptops sit on the counter below and to the right of the people, and the bottle is between the people and laptops—but it provides no direct depth, facing direction, gaze, or arm-reach measurement. The map is unreliable where labels overlap or are clipped, where a large central person mask merges body parts, and where much of the furniture, papers, and partially visible foreground body are left unlabeled.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it supplies no detected body or hand joints and cannot establish posture, facing direction, gaze, reach, or person-to-object geometry. Relative layout must therefore come from RGB and the other maps: people are partly visible ahead and to the left or right, while counters and devices occupy the nearer lower foreground. No approach, retreat, turning, limb extension, or occlusion change can be measured from this map itself across time. Its complete lack of detections is unreliable given the visible people and hands/arms in RGB, likely because bodies are heavily cropped, occluded, close to the camera, or outside the pose detector’s usable scale.
